env.saved: Saved — the API will restart briefly to apply it
env.title: Environment
env.description: A subset of the instance env vars you can change from here, without SSH into .env.dist. Saving restarts the API container briefly to apply the new values.
env.installDirBody: Set INSTALL_DIR in .env.dist to the absolute path of the folder holding docker-compose.dist.yml on this server, then restart the stack before saving from here.
env.appliedBody: The API container will restart in a few seconds — the connection to this dashboard may drop briefly, which is expected.

terminal.title: SSH Terminal (to the host)
terminal.description: The web Terminal always connects over SSH (the container cannot open a host shell directly). Fill this in to use it.
terminal.userEmpty: Not set — the terminal signs in as {user} (default).
terminal.userHint: On an Ubuntu VPS this is usually ubuntu: root login is often rejected by sshd, so use your SSH login user.
terminal.passwordOptional: optional — you can also use the platform SSH key

network.title: Network
network.description: Used for application domain DNS checks and the local registry address.

instanceBackup.title: Instance backup
instanceBackup.description: Backs up the aoox panel itself: its own database with every setting and record. It does not back up your applications' data.

included.title: Included
included.accounts: Users, members, invitations and API tokens
included.projects: Projects and the definitions of applications, stacks and databases (domains, mounts, jobs, backup schedules)
included.variables: Variable sets with their values and history
included.integrations: Registries, git credentials, servers, notifications, S3 destinations, DNS and Infisical connections, SSL certificates, Traefik config files
included.history: Deployment history and the audit log

excluded.title: Not included
excluded.databases: Managed database contents: use each database's backups
excluded.volumes: Application volume contents: use volume backups in the Mounts tab
excluded.proxy: The proxy's certificate and config files: save them again after a restore

instanceBackup.keepKeys: Keep ENCRYPTION_KEY and JWT_SECRET yourself: without the same ENCRYPTION_KEY, the restored credentials cannot be decrypted. A restore needs the exact same aoox version and does not touch running containers.
instanceBackup.scheduleDescription: Automatic backups. Only scheduled backups beyond the keep count are removed.
instanceBackup.restoreDone: Restore finished: {rows, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} in {tables, plural, one {# table} other {# tables}}

confirm.title: Restore instance?
confirm.description: All panel data (projects, applications, users, settings) is replaced with the contents of the backup from {date}. Running containers are not touched. Changes made after that backup are lost.

upload.title: Restore from file
upload.description: Upload the *.json.gz file downloaded from an instance backup. The aoox version (migrations) must match. All panel data is replaced.

proxy.title: Reverse proxy
proxy.description: Traefik routes domains to application containers and issues HTTPS certificates, on the aoox host or a remote server.

servers.title: Remote servers
servers.description: Other VPSs reached over SSH: where applications are deployed and Terminal targets.

environment.title: Environment
environment.description: Change some of this instance's env vars from the dashboard, without SSH.

backup.title: Instance backup
backup.description: A snapshot of this panel's database for moving servers or recovery.

domain.title: Panel domain
domain.description: Reach this dashboard and API through your own domain.

swarm.title: Docker Swarm
swarm.description: Service mode for applications (replicas, rolling updates) and the joined nodes.

update.title: aoox update
update.description: Check and apply updates for this panel itself.

panelDomain.title: Panel domain
panelDomain.description: Reach this dashboard and API through your own domain instead of IP:port. You need two DNS A records (dashboard and API) pointing to this server, and INSTALL_DIR set in .env.dist.
panelDomain.installDirBody: Set INSTALL_DIR in .env.dist to the absolute path of the folder containing docker-compose.dist.yml on this server, then restart the stack before saving a domain here.
panelDomain.appliedBody: The panel will restart in a few seconds to install the new domain — the connection to this dashboard will drop for a moment, which is expected. Reload the page at https://{host} afterwards.

proxy.title: The reverse proxy was not active — it has been started automatically
proxy.intro: The proxy (Traefik) was not running before, so it was enabled for you. The new domain is only reachable if these three things are also right — check them one by one if https://{host} still does not open after a few minutes:
proxy.dns: DNS A records for {web} and {api} point to this server's IP (check: nslookup {lookup}).
proxy.ports: Ports 80 and 443 are open to the public — both the OS firewall (ufw) and your VPS provider's firewall/security group.
proxy.cert: Wait a moment: the HTTPS certificate (Let's Encrypt) is only issued by Traefik the first time the domain is accessed, which takes a few seconds up to a minute.

restrict.label: Only allow access through the domain
restrict.description: Ports 3000 and 3001 stop listening to the outside and accept connections from this server only, so every visit goes through the proxy. This also closes the way around the sign-in rate limit that a direct call to the dashboard port offers.
restrict.needsBoth: Enter both the dashboard and the API domain to turn this on.
restrict.warningTitle: Check that the domain works before you turn this on
restrict.warningBody: If DNS, the firewall or the certificate is wrong you will not be able to open the panel at all, and the IP address will no longer work. The CLI and webhooks must use https://{api} as well. To recover over SSH: in the install folder delete the two ports: lines in docker-compose.override.yml, then run:
restrict.appliedExtra: IP:3000 stops working after the restart. Use https://{host}.

remove.title: Remove the panel domain?
remove.description: The dashboard and API go back to plain IP access. After the panel restarts (a few seconds) this page stops working at the domain: reopen the dashboard at http://SERVER-IP:3000. The reverse proxy, your applications' domains and the ACME email are left alone; turning off "Only allow access through the domain" is included.
remove.doneBody: The panel is restarting to go back to IP access. This page will stop responding for a moment; reopen the dashboard at {url} afterwards.
remove.doneBodyUnknown: The panel is restarting to go back to IP access. Reopen the dashboard at http://SERVER-IP:3000 (this server's IP address, port 3000) once it is back.

proxyCard.title: Traefik
proxyCard.description: Routes domains to application containers through Docker labels.
proxyCard.acmeOff: Automatic HTTPS certificates are off: set PROXY_ACME_EMAIL in the API, then enable the proxy again.
proxyCard.remoteSettings: Ports, the ACME email and removal of this proxy are managed under <link>Remote servers</link>.
proxyCard.remoteError: Could not read the proxy on this server
proxyCard.removeConfirmDescription: The Traefik container is deleted and every domain stops answering until the proxy is enabled again. Certificates are kept.

empty.title: The proxy is not enabled
empty.body: Enable Traefik to route domains to your applications and issue HTTPS certificates. It listens on port {httpPort} (HTTP) and {httpsPort} (HTTPS).
empty.bodyMember: Traefik routes domains to applications. An owner or admin can enable it.
empty.remote: Traefik is not installed on this server yet. Install it with its ports and ACME email under Remote servers.

danger.title: Danger zone
danger.description: Actions that take every domain on the aoox host offline.
danger.removeDescription: Deletes the Traefik container. Domains stop answering until the proxy is enabled again; certificates are kept.

proxyConfigCard.title: Dynamic configuration
proxyConfigCard.description: Your own Traefik middlewares, routers and services, attached per domain in the application's Domain tab.
proxyConfigCard.resyncHint: Rewrite all enabled files to the proxy (e.g. after a restore or when the proxy was recreated)
proxyConfigCard.resynced: {count, plural, one {# file rewritten to the proxy} other {# files rewritten to the proxy}}
proxyConfigCard.remoteNote: Not tested on remote servers yet.
proxyConfigCard.warning: Traefik rejects invalid files and aoox rolls them back, but a valid file can change the routing of every domain on this proxy. Check the result after saving.
proxyConfigCard.empty: An owner can add middlewares such as basic auth, security headers or a rate limit here.
proxyConfigCard.emptyOwner: Start from a preset (basic auth, security headers, rate limit, IP allowlist, www redirect) or write your own file.
proxyConfigCard.usedBy: {count, plural, one {# domain uses it} other {# domains use it}}
proxyConfigCard.deleteInUse: {count, plural, one {# domain still uses this file's middlewares, so it cannot be deleted. Detach them from the domain first.} other {# domains still use this file's middlewares, so it cannot be deleted. Detach them from the domains first.}}
proxyConfigCard.deleteDescription: The file is deleted from aoox and from the proxy. This cannot be undone.
proxyConfigCard.recreateDescription: The proxy on this server was created by an older aoox version, so it must be recreated once to load dynamic configuration: a few seconds without service for every domain on this proxy. Certificates and other routes are kept. This warning only appears once.

proxyConfigEditor.template:
# Traefik dynamic configuration (the "http" section only).
# Example: a response header middleware, then attach it to a domain in the application's Domain tab.
http:
  middlewares:
    example-header:
      headers:
        customResponseHeaders:
          X-Powered-By: aoox
proxyConfigEditor.recreated: The proxy was recreated once to load dynamic configuration.
proxyConfigEditor.description: Traefik dynamic configuration YAML. Only the http section (middlewares, routers, services, serversTransports) is accepted; certificates are managed in Integrations → SSL certificates. Traefik reloads the file without a restart.

proxyPresetDialog.title: Create from preset
proxyPresetDialog.description: Generates middleware YAML that is ready to save. You can edit the result in the editor before saving.

serverProxy.title: Proxy (Traefik) on this server
serverProxy.deleteTitle: Delete the proxy on this server?
serverProxy.deleteDescription: The proxy container on this server is stopped and removed. Application domains on this server stop being served until the proxy is enabled again.

servers.title: Remote servers
servers.description: Other VPSs you can open from the Terminal page over SSH. By default the aoox key below is used.
servers.runOnce: Run once on each server, as the user that will be used:
servers.keyUnavailable: The platform key is not available yet.

health.monitored: {count, plural, one {# container monitored} other {# containers monitored}}

add.title: New remote server
add.description: The server must be reachable over SSH from the aoox machine.
add.name: Name
add.privateKeyHint: Leave empty to use the aoox key (just run the command from this card on the server). Keys without a passphrase only.

swarm.description: Runs applications as a service (replicas, rolling updates by the daemon) — chosen per application through Deploy mode. Databases, compose stacks and previews stay plain containers.
swarm.advertisePlaceholder: Public/private IP of the host, for other nodes
swarm.addNode: Run this on another server (with Docker installed). Applications can then run on that node: pick it per application, or let the swarm schedule them. Applications with mounts stay on this host, and images built by aoox need a registry address every node can reach.
swarm.registryWarning: The local registry address is {url} — other nodes cannot pull built images. Set REGISTRY_PUBLIC_HOST to a host address reachable by all nodes (and insecure-registries or TLS on each daemon), then re-enable the registry. Public images (Docker Hub, GHCR) are not affected.
swarm.serviceApps: {count, plural, one {# application runs as a service.} other {# applications run as services.}}
swarm.leaveBlocked: Switch the applications back to container mode first
swarm.leaveDescription: This node leaves the swarm: services running there disappear, and the swarm overlay network is removed. The proxy will be reinstalled without swarm mode.

update.title: aoox update
update.description: Check and apply updates for this panel itself — running version {version}.
update.installDirBody: Set INSTALL_DIR in .env.dist to the absolute path of the folder holding docker-compose.dist.yml on this server, then restart the stack before applying updates from here.

timedOut.title: Not back after 5 minutes
timedOut.intro: The panel may still be working, or need manual attention. Check over SSH on the server:
timedOut.manual: If the containers do not come back, run the compose command manually from INSTALL_DIR:
timedOut.docs: See the Installation documentation for full details.

confirm.title: Apply the update?
confirm.description: The panel will restart (usually 1–3 minutes) — the connection to this dashboard will drop for a moment, which is expected. This page reloads by itself once the panel is back on the new version.

version.unknown: The latest version could not be checked (this server may have no access to the registry). It is retried automatically every few hours.
version.pinned: The images are installed with tag {tag} (not :latest), so updates are not tracked automatically. Latest published version: v{latest}.
version.untracked: The installed image tag cannot be determined, so the sidebar button is not shown. Latest published version: v{latest}.
version.upToDate: You are on the latest published version (v{latest}).

overlay.title: Updating aoox
overlay.explain: The panel is unavailable for about a minute while it restarts. This is normal. This page reloads by itself, and your deployed applications keep running.
overlay.waiting: Waiting for the panel to come back…
overlay.slow: This is taking longer than usual. You can reload now, or check from a terminal with aoox update panel.

failed.title: The panel did not come back
failed.body: It has been more than 5 minutes. Check the containers on the server, for example:
failed.logs: If a container is missing or keeps restarting, its log usually says why. This page keeps checking and reloads by itself if the panel returns.

server.hostInvalid: Host must be a hostname or an IP

basic-auth.label: Basic auth
basic-auth.description: Ask for a username and password before a request reaches the application.

name.label: Middleware name
name.hint: Lowercase letters, digits and "-". Used as the file name and as name@file.

password.label: Password
password.hint: At least 8 characters. Only the bcrypt hash is stored in the file.

security-headers.label: Security headers
security-headers.description: Common security headers: HSTS, nosniff, frame deny, referrer policy.

name.label: Middleware name
name.hint: Lowercase letters, digits and "-". Used as the file name and as name@file.

stsSeconds.label: HSTS max-age (seconds)
stsSeconds.hint: 0 = no HSTS. HSTS is only sent over https.

frameDeny.label: Refuse being embedded in a frame

rate-limit.label: Rate limit
rate-limit.description: Limit the number of requests per source IP.

name.label: Middleware name
name.hint: Lowercase letters, digits and "-". Used as the file name and as name@file.

ip-allowlist.label: IP allowlist
ip-allowlist.description: Only allow certain addresses/CIDRs; everything else gets a 403.

name.label: Middleware name
name.hint: Lowercase letters, digits and "-". Used as the file name and as name@file.

cidrs.label: Address / CIDR
cidrs.hint: One per line, e.g. 203.0.113.7 or 10.0.0.0/8. The client IP the proxy sees can be the IP of another proxy in front of it.

redirect-www.label: Redirect www
redirect-www.description: Permanently redirect www to non-www or the other way round. Attach it to the domain being redirected, not to the destination.

name.label: Middleware name
name.hint: Lowercase letters, digits and "-". Used as the file name and as name@file.

direction.label: Direction
direction.hint: to-non-www: attach to www.example.com. to-www: attach to example.com (without www).
